transcript.text: bosch 24 not draining, water sitting in bottom. help

This is a common issue with Bosch dishwashers (and many other brands). Water remaining at the bottom usually indicates a blockage, a sensor error, or a pump failure. Since your model is a Bosch 24, please note that "Bosch 24" likely refers to a 24-inch wide dishwasher (standard size) rather than a specific model number. Bosch models usually look like `SHXM3...`, `SHEM3...`, or `SGU...`.

Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide, starting with the most common and easiest fixes:

### ⚠️ Safety First
• Turn off the dishwasher at the control panel.
• Unplug it from the wall outlet or turn off the circuit breaker if you need to access electrical components.
• Have towels ready—there will likely be standing water.

---

### Step 1: Check for Obvious Blockages (Most Common)
Water sits at the bottom because it can’t flow out through the drain hose or pump.

1. Remove the Bottom Rack: Look inside the tub.
2. Check the Filter Assembly:
• Bosch dishwashers have a multi-stage filter system in the bottom center.
• Twist and lift out the coarse filter (plastic mesh), then remove the fine filter (flat screen) underneath.
• Clean both thoroughly under running water. Remove any food debris, glass shards, or grease.
• Reassemble carefully—if not seated properly, it can cause drainage issues.
3. Check the Drain Area: Look around where the filter was for any large debris (bones, pits, plastic) that may have fallen in.

---

### Step 2: Check the Garbage Disposal Connection
If your dishwasher drains into a garbage disposal:
1. Ensure the disposal is not clogged. Run water in the sink to see if it drains slowly.
2. Many disposals have a plugged knockout disc inside the drain inlet where the dishwasher hose connects. If this wasn’t removed during installation, it blocks drainage. You may need to poke it out with a screwdriver (disposal must be OFF).

---

### Step 3: Inspect the Drain Hose
1. Locate the drain hose (usually behind the kickplate at the bottom front or under the sink).
2. Check for kinks, bends, or crushing that could block water flow.
3. Detach the hose from both ends (have a bucket ready) and blow through it or run water through it to ensure it’s clear.

---

### Step 4: Reset the Dishwasher
Sometimes the control board gets confused by a drainage error.
1. Turn off the dishwasher.
2. Unplug it for 5–10 minutes (or turn off the circuit breaker).
3. Plug it back in and start a new cycle.

---

### Step 5: Check the Drain Pump
If the above steps don’t work, the drain pump may be faulty or jammed.

1. Listen: During a drain cycle, do you hear a humming sound? If yes but no water moves, something is jammed in the impeller. If you hear nothing, the pump motor may have failed.
2. Access the Pump:
• Remove the kickplate (bottom front panel) using a screwdriver or by releasing clips.
• You’ll see the drain pump housing. Place towels down—it will spill water.
• Check for foreign objects (glass, plastic, bones) stuck in the pump impeller. Carefully remove any debris.
• Manually spin the impeller with your finger to ensure it moves freely.

---

### Step 6: Error Codes
Check the display for error codes like:
• E15: Water leak detected (Bosch has a built-in aqua-stop sensor in the base pan). If this is lit, you may have a leak, not just a drainage issue. Empty the base pan if accessible.
• F05/F06/F07: Drain-related errors.

---

### When to Call a Professional
• If the pump motor makes no sound at all during drain cycles.
• If the impeller is broken or damaged.
• If you’ve cleared all blockages and reset the unit, but it still won’t drain.
• If you’re uncomfortable accessing electrical components or disassembling parts.

### Quick Summary Checklist:
1. ✅ Clean filters thoroughly.
2. ✅ Check for debris in the sump area.
3. ✅ Ensure drain hose is not kinked.
4. ✅ Verify garbage disposal connection is clear.
5. ✅ Reset power to the unit.
6. ✅ Inspect drain pump for jams or failure.

model is SMS24AW01G, sorry, the 24 I meant is the display, it shows E:24. humming at the end too. slightly bad smell. will try the filter

That clarifies things significantly! The E:24 error code on Bosch dishwashers specifically means "Drainage Problem." The dishwasher tried to drain, failed, and gave up after a set time.

The humming sound you heard at the end is likely the drain pump trying to push water out against a blockage or air lock. The bad smell confirms that dirty water has been sitting in the bottom of the tub for too long (likely from previous cycles where it didn’t fully drain).

Since you’re about to check the filter, here’s exactly what to do with model SMS24AW01G:

### 1. Clean the Filter Assembly (Critical Step)
This is the #1 cause of E:24 errors.
• Remove the bottom rack.
• Twist the coarse filter (the cylindrical mesh part) counter-clockwise and lift it out.
• Underneath, there’s a flat fine filter screen. Lift that out too.
• Rinse both under warm water with a soft brush (an old toothbrush works well) to remove grease and food particles. Do not use harsh scrubbers on the fine mesh.
• Check the sump area (the hole where the filters sit) for any debris like glass, pits, or plastic that may have fallen in. Use a flashlight to look deep into the drain pump inlet if you can see it.

### 2. Clear the Drain Hose & Air Gap
If the filter is clean and E:24 persists:
• Check the air gap (if your model has one): It’s usually a small chrome cylinder on the sink deck near the faucet. Unscrew the cap and clean out any sludge inside. A clogged air gap will block drainage.
• Inspect the drain hose: Ensure it isn’t kinked or crushed behind the dishwasher. If you can access it, disconnect it from the sink drain/disposal and blow through it to check for clogs (place a bucket underneath first).

### 3. Reset the Error Code
After cleaning:
1. Turn off the dishwasher at the control panel.
2. Wait 1–2 minutes, then turn it back on.
3. Run a short rinse cycle or drain-only cycle to see if E:24 returns.

### If E:24 Returns After Cleaning:
• Faulty Drain Pump: The humming sound suggests the pump is getting power but not moving water. It could be clogged internally with debris, or the impeller (fan blade) inside may be broken. You can sometimes access the drain pump from behind the kickplate at the bottom front of the dishwasher.
• Clogged Sink Drain: If your kitchen sink drains slowly, the dishwasher will also fail to drain. Run water in the sink and ensure it flows freely.

### Regarding the Smell:
Once you fix the drainage issue:
1. Run an empty hot wash cycle with a cup of white vinegar placed on the top rack (not in the dispenser) to help neutralize odors.
2. Or, use a dishwasher cleaner tablet designed for descaling and deodorizing.

Start with the filter cleaning—it resolves E:24 in most cases. Let me know if the error comes back after you’ve cleaned everything!
filter was clogged with food and a bit of broken glass. cleaned it, drains normally now and E:24 has gone

That’s great news! It sounds like the combination of food debris and broken glass created a significant blockage that prevented the drain pump from clearing the water, triggering the E:24 error code. The humming you heard was likely the pump straining against this obstruction.

Since you’ve cleared the filter and drainage is working again, here are a few quick tips to keep it running smoothly:

• Rinse Pre-Scraping: While you don’t need to pre-rinse dishes thoroughly, make sure to scrape off large food chunks (like bones or seeds) before loading. This prevents future clogs in the filter and pump.
• Check for Glass Shards: Since broken glass was involved, take a quick look around the sump area again to ensure no tiny shards remain that could damage the pump impeller later.
• Run a Cleaning Cycle: Because of the bad smell from the standing water, consider running an empty cycle with a dishwasher cleaner or a cup of white vinegar on the top rack to help deodorize and sanitize the interior.

Your SMS24AW01G should be back to normal operation now. If you notice any unusual noises or if the error code returns during a future cycle, feel free to reach out again!
